title: For a Noetherian scheme and a complete Noetherian local coefficient ring with maximal ideal I, the residue condition IsSfbResidueConstructible (bounded constructible etale residue origin and finite Tor amplitude) is closed under isomorphisms and is a triangulated object property in the ambient completed-coefficient derived category
statement: For a Noetherian scheme and a complete Noetherian local coefficient ring with maximal ideal I, the residue condition IsSfbResidueConstructible (bounded constructible etale residue origin and finite Tor amplitude) is closed under isomorphisms and is a triangulated object property in the ambient completed-coefficient derived category. No completeness condition on the object is imposed.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1 and its following triangulatedness observation; Lemma 6.5.3 (boundedness); Proposition 6.6.11 (stratified perfect characterization), using Definition 6.3.1 and Remark 6.3.2 for the residue-field constructibility condition.

proof.text: Use the exact residue functor and its localization computation from the residue-extension module. In that module the two proved membership lemmas identify IsSfbResidueConstructible with the inverse image of the bounded constructible etale essential image. Maximality makes the residue quotient a field; flatness supplies the Tor clause of the reverse membership implication.

Bounded constructible etale complexes form a triangulated category, and their comparison through the bounded-below derived category is full and triangulated. Mathlib makes its essential image isomorphism invariant and triangulated. The inverse image under the residue functor has these same properties. Identify the two object properties pointwise and transport the instances. This replaces separate zero and shift calculations.

proof_origin.place: Following Definition 6.5.1; exact residue and triangulated essential-image argument, assembled in Lean by P5.
